stories.title: Iowa lead azide detonation
stories.summary: The United States Army detonates nearly 5 tons of degrading lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant in Middletown, Iowa, citing spontaneous explosion risks.
stories.about: At exactly 9:00 am CST on November 25, 2026, the United States Army detonated approximately 9,500 pounds (4,300 kg) of lead azide stored at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant near Middletown, Iowa. The material detonated consisted of 68 drums of lead azide, a primary explosive used to initiate munitions. The explosion sent smoke hundreds of feet into the air and the sound of two explosions could be heard miles away. The plume drifted to the south. A lead-dust plume from the explosion is predicted to travel as far as 100 miles (160 km) from the detonation site and potentially into the Mississippi River.

stories.title: Pete Edochie
stories.about: Chief Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie MON, popularly known as Pete Edochie, was a Nigerian actor. He rose to prominence in the 1980s with his portrayal of Okonkwo in a Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe's novel Things Fall Apart. He began his career as an administrator and broadcaster and later became a leading actor and has received several honours, including the Industry Merit Award from Africa Magic, a Lifetime Achievement Award from the Africa Film Academy, and the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger conferred on him in 2003 by President Olusegun Obasanjo.

stories.title: Ramayana: Part 1
stories.about: Ramayana: Part 1 is a 2026 Indian Hindi-language epic mythological film directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. Produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, the film is based on the Hindu epic Ramayana by Valmiki. It is the first instalment of a two-part film series, with Part 1 being based on the first three kāṇḍa (chapters) of Ramayana, which chronicle the life of Prince Rama from childhood up to his adventurous 14-year exile. The first part features an ensemble cast that includes Ranbir Kapoor, Yash, Sai Pallavi, Ravi Dubey, Anupam Kher, Lara Dutta, Shobana, Kajal Aggarwal, Rakul Preet Singh, Vivek Oberoi, Kunal Kapoor, Arun Govil, Adinath Kothare.
